summary: The pilot-hole wall finding is fixed. I rebuilt the bracket and sliced it at the entry (back, bed) face: servo_lead_in now gives a 0.4 mm chamfer for the 2.60 mm PETG pilot holes, the window is 42.10 x 21.40 mm at y = 0, tapers to the nominal 41.30 x 20.60 mm by y = 0.4, and the thinnest wall to a pilot hole is 2.400 mm at the face (2.80 mm behind the chamfer), so it meets the 2.4 mm rule. The new test checks the same wall, and the iface tests pass (21/21). The rest of the rig is still sound: no interference, all 12 M3 fasteners aligned, the +/-90 deg sweep is clear, and arm_torque (0.54 of 4.7 kg*cm), bracket_fea (0.67 of 13 MPa), arm_fea (4.58 of 24 MPa, 0.75 mm tip deflection) and rig_mass (188 of 250 g) all pass. The renders show nothing wrong. What remains is minor: the engine still has no access checks, the catalog servo tab and boss dimensions are still unverified, and DESIGN.md quotes the old pilot and chamfer sizes.

findings.issue: Still open: nothing in the engine checks assembly access. PLAN.md's 'Assembly-access checks' item is still unchecked and kerf/ has no hex-key or insertion-path sweep. The servo, tabs and boss did not move in this change, so the earlier probe result still holds: a straight 3 mm hex key along the two cable-end tab screw axes overlaps the cable boss, and DESIGN.md step 3 covers that with a ball-end driver. kerf check would still miss the same problem on the next project, and would also miss a servo that cannot pass its window bottom-first.
findings.fix: Finish the PLAN item: (a) sweep a hex-key cylinder along each male fastener axis from the head side and flag screws that need a ball-end driver; (b) sweep parts that declare an `insert:` path into their seat and report collisions. Test both: this rig's cable-end screws must be flagged as ball-end, and a bottom-first MG996R through a tight window must fail.

findings.issue: Still open: the catalog still marks the MG996R tab-hole pattern (49.5 x 10 mm, 4.2 mm holes, 2.5 mm tab) and the cable-boss geometry UNVERIFIED. Every tab hole, the window-to-hole wall measured above, and the ball-end driver note depend on these values. DESIGN.md already tells the owner to check them with calipers.
findings.fix: With a real MG996R in hand, measure the tab-hole pattern, the tab thickness and the boss. Record the measurements in catalog/hardware.json, citing the measurement as the source, then rebuild. The lead-in will re-size itself from the new hole positions.

findings.issue: New: DESIGN.md describes the old numbers. Sizing says '2.72 mm pilot holes', but the built PETG bracket uses the catalog's self_tap_pilot_petg value of 2.60 mm (2.72 is the PLA value). It also says '0.5 mm x 45 deg lead-in chamfer', but servo_lead_in now cuts it to 0.4 mm to keep the 2.4 mm wall. The geometry is right; only the record is out of date, and someone drilling out or checking holes from DESIGN.md would use the wrong numbers.
findings.fix: In DESIGN.md Sizing, change the pilot to '2.60 mm (PETG HF vertical; catalog fdm_holes.M3.self_tap_pilot_petg)'. Change the window line to 'lead-in requested 0.5 mm, reduced automatically to 0.4 mm so the wall to the tab pilot holes stays >= 2.4 mm (ENGINEERING section 5)'.
